newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard repeats higher growth needed for jobs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard repeats higher growth needed for jobs.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Thursday the economy needed to grow faster to make a big impact on the unemployment rate.
Speaking before the release of Thursday's employment data, Howard told reporters he was confident the economy would grow at 3.5 percent in 1996/97 (July-June).
Howard said on Wednesday that 4.0 to 4.5 percent growth was necessary to tackle unemployment.
"We do need to promote faster and stronger and sustainable growth in Australia. To make a big impact on the unemployment rate you need to grow the economy at a faster rate," he said.
After he spoke, the Bureau of Statistics released figures showing employment fell 7,200 in February and unemployment rose to 8.8 percent from 8.6 percentin January.
Howard said low inflation, industrial reform, historicaly high business investment and low interest rates were positive for economic growth.
"It has always been the case that the way you create more jobs is...to have more economic growth, there is nothing revolutionary about that," he said.
"We anticipate about 3.5 percent and all the indications at the moment is that that will be achieved," Howard said.
